key_insight: Stacking ensembles outperformed the multitask neural network for all three welding-property predictions, with the largest improvement in ultimate tensile strength (UTS).
engineering_relevance: Predicting UTS, weld hardness, and heat-affected-zone (HAZ) hardness can support welding-process assessment and structural-integrity decisions.
method: Train a multitask neural network with shared representations and task-specific outputs.
Compare against stacking ensemble learning on the same dataset.
Evaluate each target using RMSE and R².
evidence_signal: Stacking versus multitask R² was 0.9863 versus 0.6724 for UTS, 0.9782 versus 0.9215 for weld hardness, and 0.8453 versus 0.8407 for HAZ hardness.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify dataset size, validation design, or RMSE units/scaling, limiting assessment of deployment readiness.
paper_title: A Comparative Analysis of Multitask Neural Networks and Stacking Ensemble Learning for Predicting UTS, Weld Hardness, and HAZ Hardness in Welding Applications
